findings.title: Scope and non-goals mirror the slice plan entry 210 exactly
findings.description: All seven scope bullets of plan entry 210 (`200-slices.developer-onboarding.md:195-200`) appear in the slice's Technical Scope with matching specifics: `VALID_TARGETS` extension, `isManagedCopilot` marker convention, the four-path worktree propagation block, guides-side `scripts/setup-ide` backend, `paths[]` → `applyTo` comma-string translation with `**` default, unchanged `cf init` detection matrix, and the additive-only write set ("never to `.claude/` or `CLAUDE.md`", line 17). The plan's ordering caveat (instruction files combine with no guaranteed order) is correctly converted into a design decision — always-on content compiled into a single `.github/copilot-instructions.md` + `AGENTS.md` (lines 58-84). All four plan non-goals are preserved in "Not included" (lines 51-55), and the dependency stance (`dependencies: []` in frontmatter; `interfaces: [202-smart-cf-init-composition]` as the consumer of `setupIdeAction`) matches the plan's "Dependencies: None".

findings.title: No scope creep beyond the architecture's composition principle
findings.description: The design honors the parent plan's Notes principle ("Composition over new infrastructure... No new storage backends, no new protocols, no new package boundaries"): CF core only validates the target, checks guide installation, performs the managed-marker check, shells out, and propagates — while compilation stays in the ai-project-guide submodule, matching how slice 177 delegated the 400+ line bash script. The explicit "No changes to" list (init.ts, `packages/core/`, `packages/mcp-server/`) is proportionate; the "Not included" list correctly defers Cursor (Future Work #1) and bidirectional sync. Mechanism count is minimal — one new helper, one new target branch, one script backend.

findings.title: Failure modes of the new I/O path are enumerated, not TBD
findings.description: The Risks section addresses the two failure modes of the shell-out path concretely: missing `copilot` case in the guide script fails at the script step "with a clear error" (consistent with slice 177's established `UserError` contract for script-not-found and non-zero exit, `177-slice.ide-setup-command.md:106-108`), and the CF-invented managed-marker convention degrading if VS Code strips comment markers is analyzed down to its consequence ("worst case is a more verbose re-run experience, not data loss"). Test coverage additionally pins the no-guides error, unmanaged-file prompt, and `--yes` bypass (lines 121-127).

findings.title: No NFR restatement required — parent architecture states none for this path
findings.description: The parent architecture (`200-arch.developer-onboarding.md`) states no measurable NFR targets (latency, throughput, etc.) on the `setup-ide`/init path — its Technical Considerations cover detection edge cases, skill maintenance, and `cf next` hot-path cost, none of which this slice touches. There is therefore no NFR that needed restating with a specific target.

findings.title: Managed-marker overwrite protection covers only 2 of the 4 Copilot write targets
findings.description: The slice declares (line 17) that the Copilot target writes to `AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/`, and `.github/prompts/`, but the safety check — `isManagedCopilotFiles(projectPath)` "checks marker in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `AGENTS.md`" (line 109; sequence step 4, lines ~99-100) — guards only the first two. Nothing defines the overwrite policy for `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` and `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`: if a user has hand-authored instruction/prompt files there, step 5 (the script run) can overwrite them with no prompt and no backup. The parent plan's success criterion is unqualified: "Re-running on a project with existing unmanaged files prompts before overwriting (same safety as Claude path)" (`200-slices.developer-onboarding.md:214`). This also conflicts with the project principle "Never use silent fallback values. Fail explicitly." Fix is one sentence: either extend the marker/backup policy to the two directories (per-file check, or an explicit "directories are CF-owned, backed up on first collision" rule), or state the script-side per-file policy the guide backend implements — but the design must specify it, since the plan criterion leaves it unmet as written.

findings.title: Tool-guide deliverable from the plan's success criteria is dropped
findings.description: Plan entry 210's success criteria require the tool guide be "referenced in slice design, promoted to a proper published tool guide if needed" (`200-slices.developer-onboarding.md:218`). The slice design does not reference `user/tool-guides/copilot-vscode/setup-ide.md` at all — no docs task, no test-coverage line. The existing file is a raw AI-chat capture (a Perplexity answer with citations), not a published guide, so the "promoted if needed" clause is likely active — especially since the slice's own Value section names an external user as the driver, and that user needs instructions for the new flow. This is a small, cheap deliverable to add back; dropping it leaves the plan criterion partially unmet without a stated reason.

findings.title: Worktree propagation writes have no stated overwrite policy
findings.description: Sequence step 6 runs `propagateToWorktrees(project, 'copilot')` after the root-level managed check, satisfying the plan criterion that propagation copies to all registered worktrees "after root setup-ide" (`200-slices.developer-onboarding.md:215`). However, the slice doesn't state whether per-worktree copies respect the managed-marker/backup policy or are silent writes, nor whether propagation still runs when the user declined the root overwrite prompt. Two unspecified behaviors on a write path that multiplies by the worktree count; one clarifying sentence would pin it.

findings.title: "Unless it lands cleanly" clause on custom agents is an unlocked conditional
findings.description: "Not included: Copilot custom agents translation (... defer implementation unless the instruction + prompt layer lands cleanly)" matches the plan's non-goal wording, but the escape clause has no criterion — it leaves the door open to pulling agent translation into this slice mid-flight. Deferral is the conservative and correct call (the plan's table also hedges with "implement if backend is stable"); consider making the deferral unconditional here and recording agent translation as its own follow-up.

findings.title: Skill → prompt-file frontmatter translation contract is unspecified
findings.description: The plan's file-mapping table lists the prompt-file frontmatter surface (`name`, `description`, `argument-hint`, `agent`, `model`, `tools`), but the slice only shows file-layout examples and gives no mapping rule for skill frontmatter (which has no `argument-hint`/`agent`/`model`/`tools` equivalents). The `applyTo` translation gets a dedicated design-decision section; this one doesn't. The guide-script implementer will have to invent defaults — which the project rules forbid ("Do not hard-code magic defaults", "Never use silent fallback values"). One line (e.g., "skill `name`/`description` carry through; unsupported fields omitted, never defaulted") closes it.

findings.title: Helper described with two different signatures
findings.description: Technical Scope introduces `isManagedCopilot(filePath)` (line 29) while Files Changed names `isManagedCopilotFiles(projectPath)` checking two files (line 109). Same convention, different shape — trivial editorial drift, but worth unifying to one name and signature so the implementation and tests reference a single definition.
